subject: Hybrid streaming + sync fallback SLA request — PolarHealth POC
messages:
From: Elena Ross <elena.ross@polarhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Angela Mayer <angela.mayer@aws-marketplace.com>
Date: Sun, 24 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: SLA ask: hybrid streaming + sync fallback (PolarHealth POC)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the call earlier. To get procurement moving we need a clear SLO matrix for the POC that covers both streaming endpoints (recommended for our user flows) and a synchronous fallback if streaming degrades. Key points PolarCare needs documented:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming endpoints (small responses like summaries, <=32 tokens) — want a 95th percentile target and a clear measurement method.
- Sustained token/sec expectations for streaming when a single session emits long outputs (we need a lower-bound during sustained generation).
- Behavior and commitments when we failover from streaming to non-streaming (what changes in latency guarantees and how queued requests are handled).
- Regional failover implications (we're US primary but will occasionally route through EU for DR).
- Monitoring hooks / metrics we can scrape (or a webhook) so our SREs can alert on regressions.

I've attached our internal requirements and a one-page SLO spreadsheet. Procurement would like these numbers firmed up before we sign the POC order. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit and what carveouts apply?

Also flag any known cold-start behavior that could affect first-minute POC traffic.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ross
Head of Product — PolarHealth
Attachment: polarproof_sla_requirements.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: slo-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ross <elena.ross@polarhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 11:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA ask: hybrid streaming + sync fallback (PolarHealth POC)

Hi Elena —

Thanks — we can and want to be prescriptive here. Below is a Redwood proposal (95th percentile unless noted):

1) Streaming endpoints (primary):
   - TTFT (<=32 tokens): 95th <= 250 ms measured at edge egress (client-observed first byte).
   - Sustained emit rate: 95th >= 60 tokens/sec per session for sustained outputs (after KV-cache warmup).
   - Availability target: 99.5% for streaming endpoint tier in the POC (we'll provide token-level SLA windows).

2) Sync fallback (when streaming is unavailable or a customer chooses non-streaming):
   - End-to-end completion for payloads <=64 tokens: 95th <= 700 ms.
   - Availability target: 99.9% for synchronous endpoints.

3) Failover & region notes:
   - If we route to EU for DR, add a measured regional delta: expect +100–200 ms on TTFT at 95th depending on routing; we will expose the route in telemetry.
   - Cold-start carveout: model shard warmup (cold KV-cache and kernel JIT) can add up to 150–400 ms for the first request after scaling events; we propose a 90s warmup window where these measurements are excluded from SLO reporting.

4) Measurement and telemetry:
   - We will provide Prometheus-compatible metrics (ttft_p95, tokens_per_sec_p95, region_route) and a webhook for incident alerts.
   - We'll also provide a lightweight SDK snippet for exact client-side TTFT measurement so PolarHealth can compute identical percentiles.

5) Operational plan:
   - 3-week canary on a dedicated pool (small reserved capacity) to validate real traffic patterns and tune batching/quantization.
   - If the canary meets targets, we'll roll to production with an A/B rollout and automated rollback if regressions exceed thresholds.

If these numbers look good, I can route a DocuSign amendment for the POC that includes the cold-start carveout language and the telemetry obligations. Karthik/Monica — please review and flag anything legal/contract that needs different phrasing.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Product & GTM — Redwood Inference
--
Note: Sustained token/sec figures assume continuous generation >8s; short bursts may show higher instantaneous throughput but won't be used for SLO calculations.

I've attached a cleaned version of our SLO matrix with the language procurement prefers. Can you send the amendment and an initial Grafana dashboard JSON? We want to sign the POC this week.

Elena
